sections.text:
Elisha, peace be upon him, is a noble prophet from among the righteous prophets of the Children of Israel. God mentioned him twice in the Holy Qur’an, and praised him, saying: “And Ishmael, and Elisha, and Jonah, and Lot, and each of them We favored over the worlds.”

The story of Elisha begins when he was a young boy suffering from a severe illness, so the Prophet Elias, peace be upon him, passed by him while he was hiding from his oppressive people.

Elisha's family sheltered the Prophet Elias in their house, so Elias prayed to God to heal this sick boy.

God answered Elias’ prayer, and Elisha was completely healed and rose as if nothing was wrong with him. From that moment, Elisha believed in Elias with love and certainty, and decided to accompany him and never leave him.

Elisha accompanied Elias in all his travels, learned the Torah from him, gained wisdom from him, and witnessed his patience and fortitude in the face of the tyranny of the king and the priests of the idol of “Baal.”

When the time of the Prophet Elias came or God raised him to it, he left Elisha to be his successor among the Children of Israel, and God inspired him with prophecy so that he would carry the banner of monotheism after his teacher.

Elisha was distinguished by great wisdom and calm, and he adhered to the law of the Torah (which was revealed to Moses) and Elias’ approach to preaching.

In his time, there were many kings among the Children of Israel, and they were divided and fought over power, which made them weak before their enemies who coveted their land.

Elisha stood strong to remind them that their disunity and abandonment of God’s teachings was the reason for their weakness and defeat.

Elisha was moving between the cities of the Children of Israel, reconciling relations, judging between them justly, enjoining good and forbidding them evil, and warning them against the worship of idols that had spread among them again.

Among the stories told about his miracles and miracles is that the people of the city of Jericho (or a city close to it) complained to him about the badness of their land and the corruption of its water.

Their water was salty and bitter, killing plants and causing diseases, so they asked Elisha to solve this problem for them.

Elisha ordered them to bring a new bowl containing salt, and they were surprised because salt spoils the water even more!
But Elisha went to the spring from which the water came out, threw salt into it, and prayed to God Almighty. Suddenly, the salty water was transformed by God’s power into fresh, clear water suitable for drinking and agriculture, and the city flourished and life returned to it!
Stories are also told about him healing the sick and plentiating the little food for the needy with the blessing of his supplication to God.

But despite his miracles and advice, the children of Israel sometimes rebelled against him, so he warned them of God’s punishment if they insisted on disobeying them.

Elisha warned them that God would place cruel kings and enemies who would have no mercy on them if they did not repent and return to the truth.

His warning was later fulfilled when the Assyrians invaded them and took away their king because of their deviation from God’s path.

Elisha continued his preaching and renounced polytheism until God took his death. He was a great sheikh, esteemed and respected among the believers of his people.

It was said that before his death, he appointed Dhul-Kifl as his successor to take his place in the judiciary and advocacy, as we saw in the story of Dhul-Kifl.

The lesson of the story of Elisha, peace be upon him, is the importance of adhering to the correct approach left by the prophets, and that social reform begins with reforming hearts and uniting God, and that blessing comes with obedience and certainty.
